scenes.title: Where and when
narration: Soukous traces its roots to the Congolese rumba of the early 20th century, which blended local maringa dance with Cuban son.
In the 1960s, musicians began accelerating these rhythms.
Orchestre Sinza Kotoko is credited with pioneering the soukous style in Brazzaville around 1966, emphasizing the sebene and energetic dance sections.

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: It is a pillar of weddings, malakis (popular festivals), and community ceremonies.
It serves as a medium for social commentary, love, and national identity.
Today it is a living tradition.

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: The dance is characterized by rapid hip movements and shifting body weight between the legs.
It is a high-energy, often partnered dance that encourages freestyle movement during the sebene section.
Dancers follow the fast-paced percussion and the lead guitar's improvisations.
Watch for Hip Shaking.
on_screen: Hero video full screen, 30–45 s (XS4ErzpF9uw)
Captions name each signature move as it appears
Formation: Freestyle; dancers often occupy space in clubs or dance halls.

scenes.title: Step B — the next layer
